top_choice_rationale: Buchwald and Hartwig built general Pd-catalysed C-N coupling on one clear principle, ligand control over amine binding, deprotonation and the difficult C-N reductive elimination, with quantitative mechanistic backing and about thirty years of independent confirmation. It is a distinct discovery from the 2010 C-C prize, the attribution is a clean pair, and the citation can be anchored to the general catalytic method so Kosugi and Migita's stoichiometric tin chemistry is not a priority issue. The ionizable lipid proposal is scientifically strong and highly consequential, but its trio is contested (Hope and Madden are regarded as essential by some members) and cannot yet be defended from the primary record, so I rank it second. A prize is still better than no award.
